title: A record-change flow's start condition is not evaluated on the re-entrant dispatch its own write causes — the loop-breaker is the only thing stopping the loop, and it says so itself (17.0.0 GA)
body:
Part of objectstack-ai/hotcrm#701. Measured live on `@objectstack/*` **17.0.0 GA**, user-driven REST writes against a booted dev server.

Searched first: #4862 (predicate bulk writes: `previous` unbound, `record` a bare payload) is closed and is a different path — this is the ordinary single-record `record-after-update` path.

## Symptom

A record-change flow whose start condition, **as authored, evaluates false on the flow's own write**, is nevertheless re-dispatched for the same record; the engine's last-resort loop-breaker catches it and logs:

```
2026-08-14T13:14:39.075Z WARN [automation] flow 'case_escalation' re-entered for the
same record while still running — breaking self-trigger loop; the triggering record's
id is in this record's meta. Its start condition did not suppress the re-fire; if it
guards on a boolean field (e.g. `is_escalated != true`), note booleans persist as 0/1
on SQLite/libsql and CEL `1 != true` is true.   {"recordId":"v5_h-3H_CbMj6jag"}
```

The message's own words are the report: *"Its start condition did not suppress the re-fire."*

## Why the guard should have held — measured, not asserted

The reporting app's `case_escalation` gates on `status` **strings** and a `null` check, not on the boolean the WARN's hint is about, so the SQLite `1 != true` explanation does not apply here:

```
condition: has(record.priority) && record.priority == "critical"
  && (!has(record.escalated_date) || record.escalated_date == null)
  && (!has(record.status)
      && record.status != "escalated" && record.status != "resolved" && record.status != "closed")
```

Record state at the moment of the re-fire, read back from the API:

```
status=escalated  is_escalated=true  escalated_date=2026-08-14T13:14:38.628Z

  record.status != "escalated"   -> false
  record.escalated_date == null  -> false
```

Both terms false. The condition as written cannot be true on that dispatch, yet the dispatch happened and only the breaker stopped it.

## Probe design (so a green could not be vacuous)

Three things asserted together, because "the flow terminated" cannot distinguish the two mechanisms:

1. the flow **actually fired** (record reached `status=escalated`) — otherwise a missing WARN proves nothing;
2. a loop-breaker WARN **carrying that record's id** (the log is filtered by the probe's own id, so unrelated WARNs cannot be miscounted);
3. the guard terms evaluated at the re-fire.

## Second flow, same shape

```
created crm_opportunity RnrCSh-5GvgPkzSM  amount=1000
PATCH amount=250000 (crosses the large-deal threshold) -> HTTP 200
  approval_status=pending
loop-breaker WARNs naming RnrCSh-5GvgPkzSM: 1
  WARN [automation] flow 'opportunity_approval' re-entered for the same record while
  still running — breaking self-trigger loop; ...
```

Its gate excludes deals already `pending`; its own write sets `approval_status = pending`; the breaker still fires.

Also reproduced **unprompted** during the platform's own seed sweep on a fresh boot — three occurrences on `case_escalation` (record ids `foDLsXSrb6CKOKbe`, `hIICKFaqJ1q_DuZD`, `hN6omYKfEla8E9EV`). Not user-context specific.

## Why it matters even though nothing runs away today

The breaker holds — one WARN per occurrence, no runaway, no corruption. The defect is that **the guard flow authors write is not the mechanism preventing the loop**, and nothing tells them so at authoring time. Every author using a status-based re-fire guard is relying on a safety net they do not know they depend on, and the net's scope is narrow by construction: it is keyed on `flowName::recordId` *while still running*. Anything outside that window — a cross-record chain, a delayed re-fire, a re-entry after the first run completes — has no second line of defence, because the first line was never actually running.

Two candidate readings, both worth naming since they need different fixes:

- the re-entrant dispatch **skips** condition evaluation, or
- evaluation **aborts** and the abort is counted as a fire.

Either way the observable contract — "a record-change flow fires only when its start condition is true" — does not hold on the dispatch a flow's own write causes.

## Repro

Any `record-after-update` flow whose data node writes a field its own start condition excludes. Create a record outside the condition, `PATCH` it into the condition, and watch the server log for `[automation] … re-entered … breaking self-trigger loop` naming that record id while the record shows the flow's own write applied.
